lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Owned the pick-path layouts for the fast-moving zone and the labor reports the shift leads used.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Put education below experience.
items.because: You have substantial post-graduate experience.

items.says: Reorder experience as Greenleaf, Crestway, then Lakeview.
items.because: Experience should be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Use one date style and en dashes for ranges throughout.
items.because: The date formatting is inconsistent.

items.says: Use a consistent number style.
items.because: “Three distribution centers” and “3 distribution centers” should follow one approach.

items.says: Keep terms such as SKUs/products and warehouses/distribution centers consistent unless the distinctions are real.
Aim for one page by reducing routine duties and generic project descriptions first.
items.because: The supply-chain work is the strongest material.

items.says: Confirm the contact details are real rather than placeholders.
Use the actual LinkedIn URL and check that its profile matches the résumé.
items.because: The titles, employers, and dates should agree.

items.says: Make the URL clickable in the submitted PDF.
Use an en dash rather than a hyphen in the date range.
items.because: Date ranges should be formatted consistently.

items.says: Remove the location if space is tight.
items.because: It adds little value.

items.says: Limit the Greenleaf entry to the most operationally relevant content.
items.because: The move from Supply Chain Planner to Delivery Driver/Shop Assistant may raise questions.

items.says: Confirm the September 2025 start date.
Confirm that the dual title is official, or use the employer-recognized title.
items.because: An unofficial title could cause background-check inconsistencies.

items.says: Use present tense for this current responsibility.
Clarify whether 30–40 arrangements is your personal daily volume on normal or peak days.
Add a performance measure such as timeliness, accuracy, or route efficiency if available.
items.because: Volume alone does not show effectiveness.

items.says: Remove the payment detail if you cannot show its accountability or scale.
items.because: It may have been incidental.

items.says: Use present tense for current work.
Add the scale or quality impact of the wedding-order work if available.
Make your specific responsibility alongside the head florist clear.
items.because: “With the head florist” weakens ownership unless collaboration is important.

items.says: Explain the operational significance of stocking and labeling.
items.because: As written, it reads as a basic task.

items.says: Describe your actual pick-path responsibility more precisely than “owned.”
Quantify the size of the fast-moving zone.
Add the effect of the layout work.
Separate the labor-reporting work if it had a distinct impact.
items.because: Combining unrelated duties makes both less persuasive.

items.says: Give the time study’s observed volume, duration, or sample size if available.
Define what “processing time” measures.
items.because: It could mean cycle time, backlog age, or end-to-end turnaround.

items.says: Clarify your role in implementing the triage station.
items.because: The bullet only establishes your role in producing findings.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and whether the 12 carriers were all carriers or a subset.
Add an effect on detention fees, dock utilization, or on-time unloading if available.
Clarify whether you also coordinated adoption and enforcement of the rules.
items.because: “Wrote the rules” may not describe your full role.

items.says: Split or sharply reduce this bullet.
items.because: It combines at least five unrelated responsibilities and is difficult to scan.

items.says: Tie cycle counting directly to the inventory-accuracy result.
Remove or separately quantify the night-shift, safety, hiring, and certification duties.
Do not imply that every listed activity raised inventory accuracy.
items.because: The causal relationship is unclear.

items.says: Explain what “2,000 highest-value locations” means.
items.because: Locations are not usually described by value without reference to the inventory stored there.

items.says: Clarify the period and method used to measure the accuracy increase.
Verify that the stockout and inventory figures cover comparable periods and account for other major causes.
Clarify whether you designed, implemented, or managed the planning model and process.
items.because: Your level of ownership is unclear.

items.says: Define “stockouts” and what the $1.9M inventory figure represents.
items.because: It could refer to average inventory, period-end inventory, or working capital.

items.says: Add the dollar value, annualized savings, shipment volume, or number of suppliers or lanes if available.
Clarify whether you designed, negotiated, implemented, or monitored the milk runs.
Specify the comparison period for the 15% saving.
items.because: Fuel rates and volume changes could affect the comparison.

items.says: Give the SKU count or reference the portfolio size consistently.
Add a measurable business result if available.
items.because: The bullet describes activity rather than impact.

items.says: Clarify whether the reorder points were implemented in a system and regularly maintained.
Explain the purpose of the monthly reviews.
items.because: The bullet merely notes the meetings.

items.says: State what the scorecard measured and how its data influenced decisions.
Add the result of renegotiating delivery windows if known.
items.because: The bullet stops at an action rather than an operational outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether all 40 vendors were in your scope and the scorecard identified the five least reliable.
Correct or remove the 112% OEE claim.
items.because: Standard OEE cannot exceed 100%.

items.says: Quantify the changeover and micro-stop improvements separately if reliable.
Explain why a supply chain planner owned packaging-line improvement work.
Recalculate or redefine the claim that lead time halved while throughput stayed constant and WIP doubled.
items.because: Under Little’s Law, doubling WIP at constant throughput would generally increase flow time.

items.says: Remove “to keep pickers busy” unless its economic benefit can be shown.
items.because: It suggests utilization was prioritized over flow and inventory.

items.says: State the customer or financial outcome if the corrected claim remains.
Confirm that “Independent Project” accurately describes the arrangement.
items.because: Work with the grocer might instead be consulting, volunteer work, or a client project.

items.says: Ensure you have permission to disclose the grocer’s operating data and results if confidential.
Distinguish completed work from ongoing work through tense and dates.
items.because: The project is listed as ongoing.

items.says: List relevant technical tools beyond Python if genuinely used.
items.because: Optimization, mapping, or data-processing tools could better describe the work.

items.says: Explain whether the current-route baseline used comparable stops, constraints, traffic assumptions, capacities, and service windows.
items.because: The 18% comparison is meaningful only if the routes are comparable.

items.says: State whether the 18% mileage reduction was modeled or realized.
items.because: It currently appears to be a planned result.

items.says: Clarify the optimization constraints and method.
items.because: They demonstrate technical depth.

items.says: Define what “within 5%” measures and whether estimates were above or below actual drive times.
Clarify whether validation used out-of-sample logs.
items.because: The same logs may have been used to calibrate the model.

items.says: Distinguish drive time from total route time.
items.because: Total route time may include loading, parking, and service.

items.says: Include the number of routes or observations if it is more informative than four weeks.
Add the pilot outcome if the month has concluded.
Clarify if the pilot is still underway.
items.because: The bullet should not imply proven operational savings.

items.says: Clarify whether you supported implementation or only handed over materials.
Make your individual contribution clear alongside “Team of 4.”
items.because: Otherwise the team size may dilute ownership.

items.says: Identify advanced Excel capabilities if they were central to the project.
items.because: “Excel” by itself is too broad.

items.says: Ensure no employer-owned methods, data, or results were improperly reused.
items.because: The project predates some Crestway work.

items.says: Replace the generic description with the areas you personally analyzed and the method used.
items.because: “Analyzed warehouse operations” gives little detail.

items.says: Remove this summary bullet if the following bullets demonstrate the work.
items.because: Generic summaries consume space without adding evidence.

items.says: Use an active construction that makes your contribution clear.
items.because: “The donation intake process was mapped” is passive.

items.says: Quantify the baseline and final intake time more precisely if possible.
Clarify how “a day sooner” was measured and whether it was sustained.
State your role in implementation as well as process mapping.
Remove or resolve the forecasting result duplicated from Crestway.
items.because: The matching scope, stockout reduction, and roughly $2M inventory result look copied or misattributed.

items.says: Do not present employer-confidential work as a volunteer-project result.
Add specific, job-relevant capabilities you genuinely have.
items.because: Two broad tool names undersell your technical background.

items.says: Describe advanced Excel or Python work through concrete competencies rather than proficiency labels.
Ensure prominent technical skills are supported by the experience and project bullets.
Use consistent capitalization.
Consider adding relevant demonstrated methods such as process improvement or transportation planning.
items.because: They may be target-job keywords that reflect your expertise.

items.says: Avoid listing basic concepts solely to increase keyword count.
